messages.text: Meetmebythesea gives McManus a first Paddy Power Gold Cup

metadata.summary: Ben Pauling’s Meetmebythesea showed his liking for Cheltenham once more and delivered owner JP McManus with his first victory in the prestigious Paddy Power Gold Cup.
metadata.content: Meetmebythesea gives McManus a first Paddy Power Gold Cup | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Meetmebythesea gives McManus a first Paddy Power Gold Cup Harry Cobden gained his biggest success in his new role with JP McManus as Meetmebythesea stormed to success in the Paddy Power Gold Cup at Cheltenham, and now bigger targets await Ben Pauling's up-and-coming star Saturday 14 November 2026 16:15, UK Image: Meetmebythesea ridden by Harry Cobden (right) on their way to winning the Paddy Power Gold Cup Ben Pauling’s Meetmebythesea showed his liking for Cheltenham once more and delivered owner JP McManus with his first victory in the prestigious Paddy Power Gold Cup. Sent off the heavily backed 2-1 favourite on his first run since winning as a novice at the Festival in March, he put in some tremendous leaps on the way round for Harry Cobden. Blueking d'Oroux, having his first run for Dan Skelton, looked the biggest danger after long-time leader Quebecois faded but Meetmebythesea powered away up the hill to win by two and a half lengths to give Cobden a second big victory in two days in the McManus colours. Pauling said: "Harry wanted to ride him forward because not many are coming from behind today and he jumped brilliantly and travelled so well. metadata.content: Carlos Adames fights Gerome Warburton as Denzel Bentley targets shot at WBC middleweight world champion next year | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Carlos Adames fights Gerome Warburton as Denzel Bentley targets shot at WBC middleweight world champion next year Carlos Adames returns to action against Wales' Gerome Warburton in Riyadh on Saturday; London's Denzel Bentley is looking to challenge Adames for the WBC middleweight world title next year; Watch Adames fight Warburton live on Sky Sports Mix from 4pm Friday 13 November 2026 20:35, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the WBC world title fight between Hamzah Sheeraz and Carlos Adames which ended in a disputed draw WBC world champion Carlos Adames fights Wales’ Gerome Warburton on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Mix from 4pm. Adames is the reigning WBC middleweight world champion but is tuning up for major title fights next year with a non-title bout against Warburton at a 165lb catchweight. Adames has an impressive track record. Undefeated at middleweight he's taken top-class wins over Sergiy Derevyanchenko, Julian Williams, Terrell Gausha and Austin Williams. He was unfortunate to be held to a draw against Hamzah Sheeraz, too. Warburton, a former Welsh champion, has not operated at that level, but this fight with Adames offers him a route to the elite end of the division, if he can score an upset.
